_note: NBC 2016 Part 4 Table 4 (Capacity Factors) and Table 5 (Travel Distance), digitised verbatim from standards/NBC2016-Part-IV.pdf (pdfplumber page index 30 for Table 4, page index 31 for Table 5 -- printed page numbers 31 and 32). Row groupings were confirmed by rendering both pages to images and reading the curly-brace merged-cell groupings directly off the page (pdfplumber's linear text/word extraction alone does not disambiguate which occupancy rows share a merged value, so row->value assignment here is taken from the visual brace grouping, not guessed). Table 4 columns: 'stairways' and 'level_components_and_ramps' (doors, corridors, ramps), both in mm per person, per NBC Table 4 note '(3)'/'(4)'. Groups Residential (A) and Educational (B) share one merged cell (10 / 6.5); Groups Assembly (D), Business (E), Mercantile (F), Industrial (G) and Storage (H) share one merged cell (10 / 6.5); Institutional (C) and Hazardous (J) each have their own distinct value. Table 5 columns are 'types_1_and_2' and 'types_3_and_4' (construction type), in metres. For Industrial the table further splits by sub-group (G-1/G-2 vs G-3); Industrial sub-groups, Storage and Hazardous all carry 'types_3_and_4': 'See Note 3' because NBC Note 3 on that page states 'Construction of Type 3 or Type 4 is not permitted' for those occupancies, so no travel-distance number exists in the PDF for that cell -- this is not an extraction gap, it is what the table says. Nothing was omitted; every row/column the real tables carry is represented.
